results.model_answer:
According to the Customs Act 1969, customs officers have discretionary power in the administration of service fees in the following ways:

1) An officer of customs not below the rank of Assistant Commissioner of Customs may, at their discretion, authorize the amendment of any document presented at the customs house upon payment of a fee determined by the Board (Clause 205).

2) An officer of customs not below the rank of Assistant Commissioner of Customs may, at their discretion, issue a certificate or duplicate of any customs document upon payment of a fee determined by the Board, if they are satisfied that no fraud has been committed (Clause 204).

3) The Commissioner of Customs may, from time to time, fix the period after which goods left or detained at customs facilities will be subject to payment of storage fees, as well as the amount of such fees (Clause 203).
